recognize_zh: 中央一顆受感染紅血球明顯比周圍紅血球大且顏色變淡，內含形狀不規則、伸出偽足樣的藍色細胞質、紫紅色染色質點與金棕色瘧色素，細胞表面可見細小點狀斑點（Schüffner dots）；這是間日瘧原蟲的阿米巴樣滋養體。
features: Single infected red cell enlarged and paler than surrounding red cells
Irregular, amoeboid blue parasite cytoplasm with pseudopod-like extensions and vacuoles
Discrete magenta chromatin dot(s) within the parasite
Fine stippling of the host cell consistent with Schüffner dots
Background red cells normocytic without other parasites; adjacent small platelet
describe_en: Thin peripheral blood smear shows a single enlarged, pale red cell containing an amoeboid trophozoite with irregular blue cytoplasm, a magenta chromatin dot and fine golden-brown pigment. The host cell shows fine red stippling consistent with Schüffner dots. Other red cells are of normal size, and no crescent gametocytes or multiple ring forms per cell are seen in this field. Findings are consistent with a Plasmodium vivax growing trophozoite; parasitemia should be quantified and species confirmed (e.g., PCR or antigen test) as clinically indicated.

ddx.vs: P. ovale also enlarges the red cell and shows Schüffner dots, but the host cell is often oval with fimbriated edges and the trophozoite is compact rather than markedly amoeboid.
P. falciparum does not enlarge red cells, shows delicate rings (often multiple per cell) with Maurer clefts, and mature trophozoites are rarely seen in peripheral blood.
P. malariae infects normal or small red cells and forms compact band or basket shapes without stippling.
